pois.name: Cleveland Public Library – Louis Stokes Wing and Main Library

pois.name: New York Public Library – Stephen A. Schwarzman Building
pois.blurb: The New York Public Library (NYPL) is a chartered public library system in New York City, United States.

themeConnection.text: The New York Public Library was established in 1895 and remains a public library institution with ordinary visitor access to service areas and reading rooms at the Fifth Avenue flagship.

image.attribution: Designed by Augustus Saint-GaudensPhotographed by Edward Stevens, Clerk of Works;traced by Simtropolitan · Public domain

clue.text: Born from a mid-19th-century municipal idea of free learning, this flagship grew into a research powerhouse while still welcoming ordinary readers. Its central complex pairs a Renaissance-inspired research building with a later companion, faces a celebrated civic square, and is known for a vast rare-book and manuscript trove alongside neighborhood branches.

theme.title: Historic Public Libraries in Cities
theme.introduction: Quiet halls gather the memory of whole cities: grand reading rooms, worn steps, and shelves that have welcomed generations of curious visitors.
theme.inclusionCriteria: Include a location only when every condition is met: (1) it is an individually named, permanent public-serving library institution, such as a city, municipal, national, state, or provincial library; (2) the institution was founded, chartered, or opened for library service on or before 31 December 1899; (3) it still operates as a library at a fixed site on the date of play; (4) ordinary visitors can enter a public service area, reading room, reference room, or equivalent during published or customary hours, subject only to routine registration, identification, or bag-check requirements; (5) the site lies within the current administrative boundary of a present-day city or incorporated urban municipality; (6) the principal library facility or independently named library occupies a single mappable location with a recognizable public entrance; and (7) its principal function remains providing public access to books, periodicals, or other library collections, whether by lending, reference use, or supervised reading.
